articles.title: Over 100 Gold Miners Killed in Deadly Mine Collapse in Central Africa
articles.summary: A terrible accident at a gold mine near the border of the Central African Republic and Cameroon has left at least 107 people dead. The disaster happened on the afternoon of 18 August 2026, when the ground at a large open-air artisanal mining site suddenly gave way. Huge amounts of soil crashed down a hillside in seconds, trapping workers below. Videos shared online showed the earth moving like a fast-moving flood. Rescue teams rushed to the scene and began digging by hand to find survivors still trapped underground. The incident has raised serious concerns about the safety conditions for workers at informal mining sites across Africa.

lv1: Where did the mine collapse happen? (這次礦場坍塌發生在哪裡？)
How many people were killed in the accident? (今次意外造成多少人死亡？)
lv2: Why do you think rescue workers had to dig by hand instead of using machines? (你認為救援人員為何要用雙手挖掘，而不是使用機器？)
What does this accident tell us about the dangers of working in informal gold mines? (這次意外反映出在非正規金礦工作有什麼危險？)
lv3: Should governments shut down informal mining sites to protect workers, even if it means those workers lose their only income? Discuss both sides. (政府是否應該關閉非正規礦場以保護工人，即使這意味著工人失去唯一收入來源？試從兩方面討論。)
Who do you think is responsible for the safety of workers at informal mines — the miners themselves, mine owners, or governments? Explain your reasoning. (你認為誰應該為非正規礦場工人的安全負責——是工人本身、礦主，還是政府？請解釋你的想法。)

articles.title: Hong Kong Plans New Rules for Ride-Hailing Apps Like Uber
articles.summary: The Hong Kong government has announced plans to introduce a law to regulate ride-hailing services such as Uber. Under the proposed plan, platforms will be able to apply for licences as early as November this year, with driver and vehicle licences also opening for applications in the fourth quarter. This move comes after years of debate about whether app-based taxi services should be allowed to operate legally in the city. Supporters say legalising ride-hailing will give passengers more choices and improve transport. Critics worry it could harm traditional taxi drivers who rely on their income. The new rules aim to balance safety, fairness and modern travel needs.

lv1: What kind of services does the Hong Kong government want to create new rules for? (香港政府想為哪種服務制訂新規則？)
When can ride-hailing platforms start applying for a licence under the new plan? (根據新計劃，網約車平台最快何時可以申請牌照？)
lv2: Why might traditional taxi drivers be unhappy about ride-hailing apps being legalised in Hong Kong? (為什麼傳統的士司機可能會對網約車合法化感到不滿？)
How could legalising ride-hailing services benefit passengers in Hong Kong? (網約車合法化對香港乘客有什麼好處？)
lv3: Do you think new technology-based transport services should be allowed to compete with traditional taxis? What rules, if any, should be put in place to make this fair? (你認為新科技交通服務應否與傳統的士競爭？如有需要，應設立哪些規則使競爭更公平？)

When new technology disrupts an existing industry, who has the responsibility to help those workers who may lose their jobs — the government, the tech companies, or the workers themselves? (當新科技衝擊傳統行業，政府、科技公司或工人自身，誰應該負責幫助可能失業的工人？)

articles.title: 郵政署削減成本 逾200員工須改簽短期合約 工會批評未有事先諮詢
articles.summary: 香港郵政近日宣布節省開支計劃，要求約200名員工將現有合約改為短期合約，令員工的工作保障大為減少。工會對此強烈批評，指管理層在未有事先諮詢員工的情況下推行此舉，違反聘書上的承諾，做法有失公平。郵政署方則表示，有關員工的聘用安排將於兩年後再作檢討。有勞工界人士指出，此事反映本港公共機構在削減成本時，有時忽視員工的合理權益，促請當局保障基層工人的就業穩定性。

lv1: 郵政署要求多少名員工改簽短期合約？
工會為什麼批評郵政署的做法？
lv2: 短期合約與長期合約有什麼分別？對員工有什麼影響？
為什麼工會認為郵政署的做法違反了員工的權益？
lv3: 當機構需要節省開支時，以改簽短期合約方式減省成本是否合理？員工的就業保障與機構的財政需要，應如何取得平衡？
你認為政府機構與私人公司在保障員工權益方面，責任是否應該有所不同？為什麼？

articles.title: 告別劣質「劏房」：地區服務隊協助基層租戶順利過渡至「簡樸房」新制度
articles.summary: 香港政府推行「簡樸房」新規定，以取代環境惡劣的傳統劏房，改善基層市民的居住質素。有地區服務隊深入社區，協助低收入租戶了解新制度的要求，並協助業主完成登記手續，確保雙方能順利過渡。新規定訂明最低居住面積及基本設施標準，旨在保障租戶的生活環境。有關人士指出，部分業主及租戶對新法規仍感陌生，需要更多社區教育及支援，以確保新政策能真正惠及有需要的市民。

lv1: 「簡樸房」新制度的目的是什麼？
地區服務隊在「簡樸房」過渡期間扮演什麼角色？
lv2: 「簡樸房」新規定對基層租戶有什麼好處？可能帶來什麼問題？
為什麼有些業主和租戶需要社區人員的協助才能了解新制度？
lv3: 你認為政府規定最低居住標準是否足以解決香港的住屋問題？還需要採取哪些其他措施？
在房屋政策上，政府、業主與租戶各自應承擔什麼責任？如果三方的利益出現衝突，應如何解決？
